column3: Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew leaves both referents as pronouns; BSB explicitly names God.
The Hebrew leaves God unnamed here and describes resisting as hardening oneself against Him.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew names pillars, where BSB says foundations.
The Hebrew says the sun does not rise; BSB says not to shine.
The Hebrew pictures the sea’s heights; BSB says waves.
The Hebrew names chambers of the south; BSB says constellations.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew coordinates passing and not seeing; BSB frames them as conditional possibilities.
The Hebrew asks who will say it without explicitly adding dares.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says words with Him; BSB interprets arguments against Him.

The Hebrew pictures bitterness as something that satiates him; BSB says overwhelms.
The Hebrew asks who will summon me; BSB says Him.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says he does not know his soul; BSB interprets having no concern for himself.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says if rather than when.
The Hebrew says He covers the judges’ faces; BSB says blindfolds them.
The Hebrew presents the days’ speed and flight as past actions; BSB uses present descriptions.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says leave my face without explicitly calling it an expression; BSB says change my expression.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew presents guilt as future; BSB says already found guilty.
The Hebrew names snow water; BSB says snow.
